set_title: Myo- names: muscle vs nerve-muscle junction diseases
stem: A 4-year-old boy falls often and cannot climb stairs. To stand from the floor he places his hands on his thighs and pushes up. His calves look large and firm. Serum creatine kinase is 20,000 U/L. His maternal uncle died at age 18 of heart failure. A muscle biopsy shows no dystrophin staining.
oneliner: 4M + falls, pushes up on his thighs to stand, large calves + CK 20,000 + no dystrophin on biopsy → ?

whyNot.A: Myotonic dystrophy shows delayed grip release; he has **calf enlargement, no dystrophin**
whyNot.B: Becker has reduced dystrophin; his stain shows **no dystrophin at age 4**
whyNot.D: Lambert-Eaton occurs in adults with lung cancer; he is **4 with X-linked history**
whyNot.E: Myasthenia fluctuates with normal CK; he has **CK 20,000 and fixed weakness**

why: Absent dystrophin: a frameshift deletion in the X-linked gene. **A boy with Gowers sign, big calves and very high CK** is Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Dipstick blood, no RBCs; CK very high**

idea.rule: Boy with Gowers sign, calf pseudohypertrophy and CK in the thousands = Duchenne.

set_title: Sclerosis names: six different hardenings in brain, skin, spine, ducts and arteries
stem: A 6-year-old boy has had seizures since infancy and mild developmental delay. He has pale oval patches on his trunk that glow under ultraviolet light, and red papules over the cheeks and nose. A head CT shows calcified nodules along the ventricular walls. Echocardiography shows a cardiac mass in the left ventricle.
oneliner: 6M + infantile seizures, delay + ash-leaf spots, facial papules + subependymal nodules + cardiac rhabdomyoma → ?

whyNot.A: Multiple sclerosis is rare at 6; he has **ash-leaf spots, seizures**
whyNot.B: ALS is adult-onset motor wasting; he has **seizures and skin patches**
whyNot.C: Sclerosing cholangitis is a bile duct disease; he has **brain nodules and facial papules**
whyNot.E: Scleroderma tightens skin; his skin has **ash-leaf patches and angiofibromas**

why: Potato-like brain hamartomas (tubers) in a neurocutaneous disease. **Seizures, ash-leaf spots, angiofibromas and cardiac rhabdomyoma** is tuberous sclerosis complex.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Upper plus lower motor signs, sensation normal**

idea.rule: Seizures + ash-leaf spots + facial angiofibromas = tuberous sclerosis.
also: TSC1 or TSC2 (hamartin, tuberin), autosomal dominant

set_title: -plasia words: how cells adapt and how they go wrong
stem: A newborn boy has respiratory failure from birth. Pregnancy was complicated by severe oligohydramnios. He has low-set ears, a flattened nose and clubbed feet. Ultrasound shows both kidneys absent. Chest x-ray shows very small lungs with a bell-shaped chest, and he develops a pneumothorax.
oneliner: Newborn boy + respiratory failure, oligohydramnios, absent kidneys + very small lungs → ?

whyNot.A: Metaplasia swaps cell types; he has **lungs that are too small**
whyNot.B: Dysplasia is disordered precancerous cells; his lungs are **small but orderly**
whyNot.C: Hyperplasia means more cells; his lungs are **underdeveloped, not enlarged**
whyNot.E: Aplasia means no tissue formed; he has **small lungs that were partly formed**

why: Organ underdeveloped: without amniotic fluid the lungs never reached full size. **Small lungs from oligohydramnios in Potter sequence** is pulmonary hypoplasia.

idea.rule: Organ forms but stays small = hypoplasia; organ absent = aplasia or agenesis.
also: Bilateral renal agenesis causes Potter sequence

set_title: -uria words: what is in the urine (blood, hemoglobin, myoglobin, odd metabolites)
stem: A 40-year-old man has low back and knee pain. His urine turns dark brown after standing in the toilet for several hours. Examination shows bluish-black discoloration of the ear cartilage and sclerae. X-rays show calcified intervertebral discs. He has had this urine change since infancy.
oneliner: 40M + urine darkens on standing since infancy + black ear cartilage and sclerae + back pain, calcified discs → ?

whyNot.A: Cystinuria gives hexagonal stones; he has **ear pigment and urine darkening on standing**
whyNot.B: Hematuria shows red cells on a fresh sample; his urine **darkens after standing**
whyNot.C: Hemoglobinuria is dark at once with hemolysis; his darkens **on standing with ochronosis**
whyNot.D: Myoglobinuria follows muscle injury; his is **lifelong with black cartilage**

why: Alkali-loving acid in urine: homogentisic acid oxidizes and turns dark. **Urine darkening on standing, ochronosis and arthropathy** is alkaptonuria.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Dipstick blood, no red cells; CK very high**

idea.rule: Urine turns black on standing + dark cartilage + arthritis = alkaptonuria.

set_title: Von- names: von Gierke, von Hippel-Lindau, von Recklinghausen (two of them), von Willebrand
stem: A 4-month-old girl has a seizure after a 5-hour gap between feedings. Glucose is 28 mg/dL with high lactate, uric acid and triglycerides. The liver is palpable 5 cm below the costal margin and both kidneys are enlarged. She has a round, doll-like face.
oneliner: 4-month-old girl, fasting hypoglycemia, high lactate and uric acid, big liver → ?

options.B: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
options.D: Osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone)

whyNot.A: Causes cerebellar, retinal and renal tumors; she has **fasting hypoglycemia and a big liver**
whyNot.C: Causes cafe-au-lait spots and neurofibromas; she has **hypoglycemia with high lactate and uric acid**
whyNot.D: Needs high PTH and bone pain; she has **fasting hypoglycemia with hepatomegaly**
whyNot.E: Causes mucosal bleeding; she has **seizure from hypoglycemia with high lactate**

answer: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
why: Von Gierke: glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency stops glycogen release as glucose (glycogen storage type I). **Fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hepatomegaly** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
Osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone)
inflamed fibrous cystic bone from high PTH

idea.rule: Von Gierke = glucose-6-phosphatase; fasting hypoglycemia, lactate, uric acid, big liver.

set_title: Von- names: von Gierke, von Hippel-Lindau, von Recklinghausen (two of them), von Willebrand
stem: A 10-year-old boy has six light-brown skin macules larger than 5 mm, freckling in both axillae, and soft skin nodules. Slit-lamp examination shows iris hamartomas. His mother has similar skin findings.
oneliner: 10-year-old boy, six cafe-au-lait spots, axillary freckling, iris hamartomas → ?

options.A: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
options.D: Osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone)

whyNot.A: Causes infant hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly; he has **skin macules and iris hamartomas**
whyNot.B: Causes hemangioblastomas and renal cancer; he has **cafe-au-lait spots and Lisch nodules**
whyNot.D: A bone disease with high PTH; he has **skin macules and axillary freckling**
whyNot.E: A bleeding disorder; he has **cafe-au-lait spots and iris hamartomas**

why: Nerve fibrous tumors from NF1 gene loss (chromosome 17), described by von Recklinghausen. **Cafe-au-lait spots, axillary freckling and Lisch nodules** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage type I)
Osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen disease of bone)
inflamed fibrous cystic bone from high PTH

idea.rule: Von Recklinghausen names two diseases: NF1 (skin, nerves) and bone disease from high PTH.

set_title: Pick vs Niemann-Pick: a dementia vs a storage disease (and their storage look-alikes)
stem: A 6-month-old Ashkenazi Jewish girl has poor feeding, loss of motor milestones and massive hepatosplenomegaly. Fundoscopy shows a cherry-red macular spot, and biopsy shows lipid-laden foamy macrophages.
oneliner: 6-month-old girl, cherry-red spot, big liver and spleen, foamy macrophages → ?

whyNot.A: An adult dementia; she is a **6-month-old with hepatosplenomegaly**
whyNot.B: Shows a cherry-red spot without organomegaly; she has **massive hepatosplenomegaly**
whyNot.D: Shows wrinkled macrophages and bone pain; she has **a cherry-red spot**
whyNot.E: Shows globoid cells and no organomegaly; she has **hepatosplenomegaly and foamy macrophages**

why: Ludwig Pick described sphingomyelinase deficiency (lysosomal storage). **Infant with cherry-red spot, hepatosplenomegaly and foamy macrophages** fit.

idea.rule: Cherry-red spot: with organomegaly = Niemann-Pick; without = Tay-Sachs.

set_title: Pick vs Niemann-Pick: a dementia vs a storage disease (and their storage look-alikes)
stem: A 6-month-old Ashkenazi Jewish boy has exaggerated startle to noise, hypotonia and loss of head control. Fundoscopy shows a cherry-red macular spot. The liver and spleen are not enlarged.
oneliner: 6-month-old Ashkenazi boy, cherry-red spot, startles easily, no organomegaly → ?

whyNot.B: An adult dementia; he is a **6-month-old with hypotonia**
whyNot.C: Causes cherry-red spot with organomegaly; he has **normal liver and spleen size**
whyNot.D: Causes organomegaly and bone pain; he has **hyperacusis and a cherry-red spot**
whyNot.E: Shows optic atrophy and globoid cells; he has **a cherry-red spot and startle**

why: Tay and Sachs described hexosaminidase A deficiency, with GM2 ganglioside accumulating in neurons. **Cherry-red spot, hyperacusis and no organomegaly** fit.

idea.rule: Tay-Sachs = cherry-red spot, no organomegaly; Niemann-Pick = cherry-red spot with hepatosplenomegaly.

set_title: Pick vs Niemann-Pick: a dementia vs a storage disease (and their storage look-alikes)
stem: A 30-year-old Ashkenazi Jewish woman has bone pain, easy bruising and fatigue. The spleen is palpable 8 cm below the costal margin, platelets are low, femoral head avascular necrosis is seen on x-ray, and marrow shows macrophages with wrinkled tissue-paper cytoplasm.
oneliner: 30-year-old Ashkenazi woman, bone pain, big spleen, low platelets, tissue-paper macrophages → ?

whyNot.A: An adult dementia; she has **splenomegaly and bone pain**
whyNot.B: Causes infant neurodegeneration with foamy macrophages; she has **adult bone disease**
whyNot.C: Causes infant neurodegeneration without organomegaly; she has **splenomegaly and bone pain**
whyNot.E: Causes infant neuropathy with globoid cells; she has **splenomegaly and tissue-paper macrophages**

why: Gaucher: glucocerebrosidase deficiency fills macrophages with glucocerebroside. **Bone pain, splenomegaly, low platelets and tissue-paper macrophages** fit.

idea.rule: Gaucher = bone pain, big spleen, tissue-paper macrophages; treat with enzyme replacement.

set_title: R- eponyms: Reye, Rett, Reiter, Riedel, Richter, Raynaud
stem: A 3-year-old girl had normal early development and spoke a few words by 14 months. Over the past year she has lost her words and purposeful hand use. She constantly wrings her hands, and her head growth has slowed. She has episodes of breath-holding.
oneliner: 3F, lost words and hand use after normal start + hand-wringing, slowed head growth → ?

whyNot.A: Reye syndrome follows aspirin with a virus; she has **no liver injury or aspirin**
whyNot.B: Riedel thyroiditis is a neck disease; she has **regression and hand-wringing**
whyNot.C: Raynaud phenomenon is cold-induced finger color change; she has **developmental regression**
whyNot.E: Richter transformation affects adults with CLL; she is **3 years old with regression**

why: Named for Rett. MECP2 mutation in girls: **normal start, then lost speech and hand-wringing**.

idea.rule: Rett = girl, MECP2, regression with hand-wringing.
also: X-linked dominant; usually lethal in boys

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **CLL with sudden node growth, high LDH**
**Fingers white, blue, then red in cold**

set_title: -blastoma names: childhood tumors of immature cells
stem: A 4-year-old girl has a painless abdominal mass found by her mother during a bath. Blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg and urinalysis shows microscopic hematuria. Ultrasound shows a solid left renal mass that does not cross the midline. Urine catecholamines are normal. She has aniridia.
oneliner: 4F, smooth flank mass not crossing midline + hypertension, hematuria, aniridia → ?

whyNot.A: Medulloblastoma is a posterior fossa tumor; her mass is **in the kidney**
whyNot.B: Neuroblastoma crosses the midline with high VMA; hers **does not and VMA is normal**
whyNot.D: Glioblastoma is an adult brain tumor; she is **4 with a renal mass**
whyNot.E: Retinoblastoma is an eye tumor; hers is **a renal mass**

why: Nephro = kidney. A kidney embryonal tumor, also called Wilms: **flank mass not crossing midline, hypertension and aniridia** (WT1).

idea.rule: Wilms = kidney, WT1, aniridia, does not cross midline.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Child flank mass not crossing midline; WT1**
**Child midline cerebellar tumor; Homer Wright rosettes**
